transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well... it's mostly work issues. I'm a translator. For months now, I've been seeing this... pattern in our project files. 

Certain subcontractors and, well, one colleague in particular... they keep making these tiny changes to the translation memory. And the timestamps. Just to make it look like my quality control failed. I tried bringing it up, but IT says the audit trail is clean. But... I know what I'm looking at. I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. 

So... that's why I'm here, I guess.
How long has this feeling that your colleague and subcontractors are deliberately altering records to frame you been going on?
...About eleven months, I suppose. It started... well, shortly after they put me in charge of the new localization project at work. That's when I first noticed it.
Aside from these beliefs about your colleague, have you ever heard voices, or seen or sensed things that other people around you don't seem to notice?
No... no, nothing like that. I just... I just see what's in the files. That's all.

Over these past eleven months, have you noticed any significant changes in your mood, like feeling persistently sad, hopeless, or losing interest in things, or on the other end, feeling unusually elevated, energetic, or needing much less sleep than usual?
No... I haven't noticed anything like that. I sleep fine. I'm just... trying to do my job, really. My mood is normal.

Aside from this situation at work, how have things been going for you overall—are you still able to manage your daily responsibilities, keep up with relationships, and take care of yourself the way you used to?

Things are fine. I still... I still do my translations, manage the team's workflow. Pay the bills. Keep up with my family routines, all of that. Everything else is normal. It's really just... well, the only time things go off track is when those certain coworkers or the file histories come up. Other than that, I'm fine.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with an 11-month history of a fixed, non-bizarre delusion (belief that a colleague and subcontractors are deliberately altering translation records/timestamps to frame him), which he holds with full conviction despite contrary evidence (clean audit trail per IT). There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech or behavior, and no mood episode symptoms (no depression or mania reported, mood described as normal). Functioning outside the delusional belief system is well preserved—he continues to work, manage his team, pay bills, and maintain family routines. This pattern of an isolated, persistent, non-bizarre persecutory delusion lasting more than one month, without prominent hallucinations, disorganized symptoms, mood episode, or significant functional decline, is characteristic of Delusional Disorder (F22) rather than Schizophrenia (which requires broader symptoms and functional impairment) or a mood disorder with psychotic features (which requires mood episode criteria).
